The div's gold runs across the page." - wait: 2000 - caption: "A block starts a new line and takes the full width." - wait: 1500 - caption: "An inline box sits inside the line of text." - wait: 1500 - caption: text: "display: block makes the span act like a div." say: "Display block makes the span act like a div." - type: { into: HTML code, text: " display: block;\n", after: "gold;\n" } - expect: { selector: "#preview-text", contains: "9 am" } - wait: 2500 hook: "Some boxes start a new line and some sit inside one. Which is which decides how a page looks." --- Some parts of a page start on a new line, like a paragraph. Others sit inside a line of text, like a bold word or a link. Which kind an element is decides how it fills the page. ## Predict ```step stage: predict code: page.html#banner insight: "Students see a box as the size of its words; a block box takes the full width of the page, an inline box only its words." check: type: predict q: "Look at the gold background. How wide is it behind 9 am, and behind Bring a hat and water.?" options: - "Behind 9 am, only its words. Behind the hat line, the full width of the page" - "Only the words, in both places" - "The full width of the page, in both places" - "Behind 9 am, the full width. Behind the hat line, only its words" fault: logic misconception: block-full-width actual: "Only the words behind 9 am, and the full width behind the hat line. A span sits inside the line of text. A div is a block: it starts on a new line and takes the full width." ``` `` and `
` are tags you have not met. Both are plain boxes that the class `mark` colours gold. How wide do you think the gold will be in each place? ## Run ```step stage: run code: page.html#banner-run try: { playground: html, starter: "page.html#banner-run", height: 460, boxes: true } insight: "Block boxes start a new line and take the full width; inline boxes sit in the line; display switches one into the other." check: { type: reflect, text: "I can say why a div stacks and a span sits in a line." } unlocks: [div-box] ``` Compare the page with your prediction. Then change `span` to `div` (in the opening and closing tag): `9 am` jumps onto its own line. Change it back. The last link is an inline ``, yet it takes a whole line, because its class sets `display: block;`. Add `display: block;` to the `.mark` rule too: the span now stacks like a div. | Code | What it does | Why | |---|---|---| | `

Pick the tags that sit inside a line. ## Modify ```step stage: modify insight: "display changes how an element fits in the line, and a div groups elements so one rule styles them together." try: { playground: html, starter: "page.html#modify", height: 460 } tasks: - hint: - "Labels are inline, so each one sits beside its box." - "Add `display: block;` to the `label` rule." check: { type: code, text: "Put each label on its own line, above its box.", rules: { contains: ["display: block;"] } } expected: page.html#sol-label - hint: - "Wrap both paragraphs in one div that has the class. The div needs a closing tag after the second paragraph." - "Then write a `.packing` rule with a `background-color`." check: { type: code, text: "Group the two paragraphs in a div with the class packing, and give it a background colour.", rules: { tags: [div], contains: ["class=\"packing\"", ".packing {", "background-color:"] } } expected: page.html#sol-div ``` ### Labels on their own lines Each label should sit above its box. ### Group the paragraphs One `
